A glass tank in a thin steel frame that holds 32,000 mB of any liquid. It refuses gases, like the Fluid Tank does: those go in a Gas Reservoir.
# One big tank
Fluid Reservoirs that touch merge into one tank of any shape and size: a tower, a wall, a pool, an L. The frame runs only round its outer edges.
- It shares one liquid, filling from the bottom up: the lowest layer fills first, then the next.
- Every block of it takes and gives the liquid: buckets, conduits, pipes, an XP Drain on top.
- A comparator on any block reads the whole tank.

# Breaking one
A broken Fluid Reservoir keeps its share of the liquid on the item (a full block from the bottom, an empty one from the top); the rest settles down again. Place it back, or on another tank of the same liquid, and it joins in.
# Different liquids
Tanks holding different liquids stay apart even when they touch; an empty one joins whichever it meets. Fluid and Gas Reservoirs never join.
It was called the Reservoir before; placed ones carry on as Fluid Reservoirs.
